potato.name: Potato
potato.notes: Cool-season crop. Heat is the primary threat. Without irrigation, rainfall during tuber bulking is critical. Early varieties that mature before July avoid both heat stress and summer drought. Strongly recommended for Vojvodina given recent climate trends.

germination.note: Soil temperature at 10cm depth. Air temperature alone is insufficient — soil warms more slowly than air in spring.

frost.note: Emerging shoots are very frost sensitive. Tubers can tolerate brief light frost if well covered with soil. A late frost in April can kill emerged shoots but plants often recover from the tuber.

heat.note: Tuber initiation stops above 29C night temperature. Given Vojvodina now averages 20+ days above 35C in summer, late-season potatoes face serious heat risk.

optimal.note: Potatoes prefer cool nights. The day-night temperature difference is important for tuber quality and starch accumulation.

water.no_irrigation_risk: HIGH RISK without irrigation. July average rainfall (57mm) is well below the 120mm crop water need. Early varieties harvested by late June dramatically reduce this risk.

gdd.note: Early varieties: ~1000-1200 GDD. Medium varieties: ~1300-1500 GDD. Late varieties: ~1600-1800 GDD.

traditional_planting.note: For no-irrigation growing, early varieties planted March-April and harvested June-July are strongly preferred.

sources: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 33 and 56
Potato Association of America agronomy papers

tomato.name: Tomato
tomato.notes: Warm-season crop. Cannot tolerate any frost. Also very sensitive to extreme heat during flowering. In Vojvodina, the challenge is navigating between late spring frost risk and summer heat stress.

germination.note: Typically started indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting. Do not transplant until frost risk is very low and nights are above 10C.

frost.note: Tomatoes are killed by even light frost. Do not transplant until the 90th percentile last frost date has passed — approximately April 24 in Vojvodina.

heat.note: With 20+ days above 35C per year in recent years, fruit set failure in July-August is a serious risk.

optimal.note: Night temperatures below 10C slow growth significantly and can cause poor fruit set.

water.no_irrigation_risk: VERY HIGH RISK without irrigation. Tomatoes need ~160mm in July but Vojvodina averages only 57mm. The rainfall deficit in July alone is ~103mm.

gdd.note: Early cherry/salad types: ~1000 GDD. Main crop beefsteak types: ~1200-1400 GDD.

traditional_planting.note: Without irrigation, earlier planting allows fruit to develop in June when rainfall is higher.

sources: UC Davis Vegetable Research and Information Center

onion.name: Onion
onion.notes: Cool-season crop with good frost tolerance. Bulbing is triggered by day length — use long-day varieties for Vojvodina latitude ~45N. One of the easier crops for Vojvodina climate.

germination.note: Onions can be direct seeded very early. Commonly started indoors January-February or direct seeded in March.

frost.note: Onions are significantly more frost tolerant than tomatoes or cucumbers. Established plants survive to approximately -6C to -8C. Young seedlings are more vulnerable.

heat.note: Onions are more heat tolerant than tomatoes. Quality declines above 33C but severe stress and bolting occur around 38C.

optimal.note: Long-day varieties required at latitude 45N. Bulbing triggered by more than 14-16 hours daylight occurring naturally in May-June in Vojvodina.

water.no_irrigation_risk: MODERATE-HIGH RISK without irrigation. Onions have very shallow roots (~30cm) and cannot tolerate even short dry spells during bulbing. Early planting to complete bulbing in June before July rainfall decline is recommended.

gdd.note: Day length is as important as temperature for bulbing initiation. Use long-day varieties only.

traditional_planting.note: Early planting is key without irrigation. Getting bulbs to develop in May-June uses the better rainfall period.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.notes: Warm-season crop. Extremely frost sensitive. Cucumbers are approximately 95% water by weight — making consistent rainfall absolutely critical. Without irrigation, cucumber success depends heavily on July-August rainfall.

germination.note: Cucumbers need warm soil. Planting in cold soil causes poor germination and rotting seeds. Soil should be consistently above 15C.

frost.note: Extremely frost sensitive. Even a very light frost will damage or kill cucumber plants at any growth stage.

heat.note: Cucumbers are more heat tolerant than tomatoes during flowering, but fruit quality declines above 35C. Water stress combined with heat is especially damaging.

optimal.note: Most heat-loving of our four crops. Main risks are frost at planting time and drought combined with heat in July-August.

water.no_irrigation_risk: VERY HIGH RISK without irrigation. Cucumbers need ~160mm in July but Vojvodina averages only 57mm — a deficit of ~103mm. Water stress causes bitter fruit, poor set, and plant wilting.

gdd.note: Fast maturing relative to other crops. A crop planted in late April can be harvesting before worst July-August heat.

traditional_planting.note: Without irrigation, early planting (late April) is strongly recommended so fruit develops in June when rainfall is higher.
